concept: InputGroup is an Input with something fixed at one or both ends of the same recessed window: a word like THB or https://, a unit, or a small key such as Copy. The window stays one part with one ring, and a hairline rule shows where the typed text stops and the fixed printing begins.
family_difference: InputGroup takes a leading and a trailing add-on, a word or an IconButton, ruled off inside the one well, where Input only prints a short unit after the value.

default_to_avoid.pattern: InputGroup as a bootstrap-style input group: a grey box glued to the side of a bordered input, each with its own border and its own focus state
default_to_avoid.why_not: Two frames mean two edges and two focus states, so the person cannot tell what is typed and what is printed; here the single recess holds both.

references.source: system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the entry window is a recess in the body, with its unit printed on the case beside it

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The window is one surface.sunken with elevation.well. The add-ons sit inside it and never raise their own plate.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label stays printed above the well on the inset line, and the add-ons are printing inside the well, not labels of their own.

derivation.consequence: every part that takes the keyboard shows the same ring
derivation.form: One ring is drawn around the whole well when the text field or a key in an add-on holds focus, so the group reads as one part.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: A key in an add-on keeps its 44px disc and runs the full height of the well, so the well stays 44px tall.

options.name: printed words inside the well, no rule
raised plates butted onto the well

variants.reason: A keeps one recess and one ring, and the hairline rule tells typed text from printing (P2 depth, P3 interaction). B has no rule, so THB beside 1,250 reads as one typed string. C raises a plate that looks pressable when it is only a word, splits the window in two edges and breaks the single ring.

root.why: The field stacks its label, well and messages in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

well.why: One recess holds the add-ons and the text field, with shade on its top-left inner edge, so the group is a single window.

field.why: Typed text is primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

addon.why: A fixed word is printed in secondary ink at the label size and ruled off from the text by a hairline, so printing and typing are told apart without colour.

hint.why: The hint is secondary ink in the caption size under the well.

error.why: The error is critical red with a glyph and words, never orange and never colour alone.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means invalid is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

md.why: The default well is 44px tall so the text field and a key in an add-on both meet the 44px target.

lg.why: The large well is 52px tall with larger text, to hold the 52px key of a phone sheet.

focus-within.why: The whole well shows the same dark ring when the text field or a key inside it holds the keyboard focus.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled group loses its recess shadow and its print fades to half, so it reads as not taking input right now.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well and the rules keep real borders and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.
